guideTitle: 6 Best Machine Washable Shower Mats in 2026
metaTitle: Best Machine Washable Shower Mats in 2026
metaDescription: Six machine washable non slip shower and tub mats compared by wash instructions, suction cup count, drain holes and size, with tips to keep cups gripping.
introParagraphs: A shower mat is a grime magnet. Soap film, body oils and minerals settle on the top surface, and the underside, with its rows of suction cups, traps a layer of residue that is hard to reach with a sponge. The mat that gets washed in a machine every week or two will grip better and smell better than one that is rinsed and ignored, which is why washability is more than a convenience for a safety product.

The six mats here are the OTHWAY 27 by 27 inch square stall mat with 224 suction cups and a foldable design, the Yimobra 34.5 by 15.5 inch long mat that is machine washable and quick drying, the Yimobra 35 by 16 inch mat with 253 cups and 240 drain holes, the TEMIR with strong suction cups and a soft surface, the homerella 35 by 16 inch mat with over 250 cups that washes on a cold cycle and the GORILLA GRIP 35 by 16 inch mat with hundreds of cups.

We evaluated each on what the listing says about washing, size, grip and drainage, and on how practical it is to launder. Machine washing a suction mat is generally a cold, gentle job followed by air drying, since heat can warp cups and soften material, so we pay attention to which listings say how to do it and which only say machine washable. Read the care details on each product page before the first wash, because they differ by maker.

products.name: OTHWAY Square Shower Mat, 27 x 27 Inch, TPE With 224 Suction Cups
products.description:
OTHWAY's square mat is described as an extra large mat for a small shower at 27 by 27 inches, in premium TPE with an anti-slip textured surface and 224 strong suction cups. The listing says it is machine washable and foldable, and the folding makes it easy to store and to fit into a washing machine. It is aimed at stand-up stalls and at families with older adults.

A square mat that folds is practical for laundering, because a flat 27-inch square can be awkward to cram into a front-loader, while a folded one fits. TPE tolerates washing better than some materials and stays flexible. The listing does not give a drain hole count in the text we have.

Compared with the long tub mats here it is built for a stall, and compared with the GORILLA GRIP it states a cup count and folds. It suits a stand-up shower where a washable, foldable mat is wanted. If your machine is small, fold it once more and use a mesh bag, which also keeps the cups from catching on the drum.
products.bestFor: A stand-up stall and a mat that folds into the wash.
pros: 27 by 27 in covers a small stall
cons: Drain hole count is not stated in the text we have
Square shape does not suit a long tub

products.name: Yimobra Bathtub Mat, 34.5 x 15.5 Inch, Machine Washable, Drain Holes
products.description:
Yimobra's 34.5 by 15.5 inch mat leads with cleaning: the listing says it is machine washable for deep cleaning, and that after use you simply rinse it and hang it up, when it dries quickly. It also makes a pointed argument about drainage, noting that holes which are too small can let foam and stagnant water accumulate, which makes the mat harder to clean. The mat has drain holes sized to avoid that.

That drainage point is a useful one: a mat that holds soapy water is a mat that smells. Rinse-and-hang is a good routine, and the machine wash is the periodic deep clean. The listing describes anti-slip security on smooth tub floors and does not give a cup count in the text we have.

Compared with the other Yimobra it is a little smaller and gives no cup number, and compared with the OTHWAY it is a tub mat. It suits a household that cleans the mat often and values quick drying. A few seconds of squeezing the water out between your hands before hanging speeds up drying noticeably. If the drain holes are clear, a mat this size dries on a towel bar in a few hours.
products.bestFor: A mat that rinses, hangs and dries quickly between washes.
pros: Rinse and hang routine dries quickly
Drain holes designed to avoid foam build-up
cons: Cup count is not stated in the text we have

products.name: Yimobra Bathtub Mat, 35 x 16 Inch, 253 Suction Cups, 240 Drain Holes
products.description:
This Yimobra gives both counts: 253 powerful suction cups and 240 drain holes on a 35 by 16 inch mat, with a fine non-slip texture on the surface and large suction cups described as holding on smooth surfaces. The listing says it fits most bathtubs and that excess water and soap discharge quickly. The stated numbers make it easy to compare.

For a washable mat, drainage and cups are both part of cleaning: more holes means less trapped soap, and more cups mean more crevices to rinse. A machine wash on a gentle cold cycle suits this kind of mat. The listing does not state washing instructions in the text we have, so check the product page.

Compared with the other Yimobra it has stated cup and hole counts, and compared with the homerella it has a lower cup count but a stated hole count. It suits a buyer who wants stated numbers and a standard tub size. After a wash, press the cups against a smooth tile or the tub floor to check they still seal.
products.bestFor: Stated cup and drain counts on a standard tub mat.
cons: Washing instructions are not in the text we have

products.name: TEMIR Non Slip Bathtub Mat, Machine Washable, Strong Suction Cups

specList.label: Testing
specList.value: ASTM F462 wet slip, per listing

products.description:
TEMIR is machine washable, has quick drain holes, strong suction cups for smooth surfaces and a soft textured top that is gentle on bare feet. The listing also cites ASTM F462 wet-surface slip testing in an accredited lab. For a washable mat, the soft surface matters: a gentle top is less likely to be scrubbed raw by washing and wearing.

A soft surface and a stated test give it a different profile from the count-focused mats, though neither the cup count nor the dimensions appear in the text we have. The testing claim is the maker's, so treat it as design intent and read the scope on the product page. A weekly machine wash keeps the soft surface fresh.

Compared with the OTHWAY it cites a standard instead of counts, and compared with the homerella it has no stated mildew claim. It suits a buyer who wants a soft, washable mat with a test reference. If you machine wash it often, the soft surface will keep its feel longer on a gentle cycle than on a heavy one.
products.bestFor: A soft surface, easy washing and a test reference.
cons: Cup count and dimensions are not stated in the text we have

products.name: homerella Bathtub Mat, 35x16, Machine Washable on Cold, Anti Mold
products.description:
homerella is the listing that tells you how to wash it: machine washable on a cold wash. It adds over 250 suction cups on a 35 by 16 inch mat, an anti-mold and mildew resistant design with extra large drain holes and an odorless material suited to sensitive skin. The cold-wash instruction is exactly what a suction mat needs.

Cold water protects cups from warping, and avoiding the dryer protects the material, so a listing that names the cycle is more helpful than one that says only washable. The antibacterial and mildew claims are the maker's wording. The mat's high cup count means more crevices that benefit from a wash.

Compared with the Yimobra 253-cup mat it has a higher cup count and a wash instruction, and compared with the GORILLA GRIP it states cups and a cold cycle. It suits a household that wants clear care guidance and a high cup count. Run the machine on its cold setting and add a little mild detergent, since harsh soap can leave a film on the cups.
products.bestFor: Clear cold-wash guidance and a high cup count.
cons: Antibacterial claims are the maker's wording
Drain hole count is not stated in the text we have

products.name: GORILLA GRIP Bath Tub Shower Mat, 35x16 Clear, Machine Washable
products.description:
GORILLA GRIP's tub mat is listed as machine washable, with hundreds of suction cups, hundreds of drain holes and a BPA-free hexagon pebble-textured top in a 35 by 16 inch size. The benchmark brand does not state a cup count or washing temperature in the text we have. It is the mat many people compare others against.

A washable benchmark is reassuring because it is made to be laundered, and a clear mat shows grime plainly, which tells you when it needs washing. The pebble top rinses clean easily. As with the others, a cold, gentle cycle and air drying are sensible.

Compared with the homerella it gives less care detail, and compared with the Yimobra it is a better-known name. It suits a buyer who wants a familiar brand and a washable standard-size mat. Because it is a widely sold model, replacements are easy to find when this one reaches the end of its life.
products.bestFor: A familiar brand and a standard washable mat.
cons: Cup count and wash cycle are not stated in the text we have

buyingCriteria.explanation: Many listings say only machine washable. The homerella adds cold wash, and the Yimobra adds rinse and hang. A good routine for any suction mat is a gentle cold cycle, no dryer and air drying flat or hung. Heat can warp cups and soften material. Check the product page for specific instructions.

A 35-inch mat or a 27-inch square can be bulky, and a mat that does not fit tends to be hand-washed instead. The OTHWAY square is foldable, which helps. Put the mat in a mesh bag or a pillowcase to protect the cups and your machine. Wash it alone or with towels.

The underside of a suction mat collects soap film in each cup. The homerella has over 250 cups, the Yimobra 253 and the OTHWAY 224, which are many crevices. Washing removes that film, which keeps the cups gripping. Rinse the underside by hand between washes.

The Yimobra argues that holes that are too small trap foam and stagnant water, and its mats have 240 holes in one version. Good drainage means less to wash out. Even so, lift and dry the mat after each shower. A mat that dries quickly needs washing less often.

TPE on the OTHWAY is flexible and tolerates washing, while PVC on others is durable but can stiffen with repeated heat. A soft surface like the TEMIR is kind to feet and holds up if the wash is gentle. Expect to replace a mat after a year or two. Replace a mat that has been washed many times and now feels thin or slick, even if the cups still look intact.

A weekly rinse and a machine wash every two to four weeks is a reasonable pattern for most households, more often with heavy use or hard water. A mat that smells or feels slick is overdue. Keep a spare if you want to avoid a day without one. Set a recurring reminder on your phone for the wash, so that it does not depend on remembering to notice a smell.

howWeEvaluated.title: Care guidance
howWeEvaluated.description: We read what each listing says about washing: cold wash on the homerella, rinse and hang on the Yimobra and a foldable design on the OTHWAY square. Specific guidance earned credit over a bare machine washable label. We looked at care guidance as a feature, since a wash instruction is the difference between a mat that lasts and one that warps.

howWeEvaluated.title: Practical fit in the machine
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered the size and foldability of each mat. The OTHWAY square folds, and the 35-inch mats need a bag. We noted that bulky mats are less likely to get washed. Foldable and compact mats were credited because bulk is the main reason mats are not washed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip and drainage
howWeEvaluated.description: Cup counts of 224, 253 and over 250 and the Yimobra hole count of 240 were compared. We weighed grip with how easy each mat is to keep clean. We considered how many crevices a mat has to clean, since cups and holes both trap residue.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material resilience
howWeEvaluated.description: TPE and PVC were compared for how they handle repeated washing. We considered softness and the risk of warping. Flexible materials earned credit. Where a listing was silent on temperature, we recommended a cold, gentle cycle as the safest default.

howWeEvaluated.title: Claims discipline
howWeEvaluated.description: Antibacterial, mildew and testing claims were read as maker statements. We favored listings that explain how to clean the mat. We weighed how easily a caregiver could handle, wash and dry each mat on a regular schedule.

howToChoose.subheading: Machine Wash vs Rinse and Hang

cards.label: Machine wash
cards.text: A cold, gentle cycle in a mesh bag removes soap film from the cups and the top. Choose it every two to four weeks for the deep clean.

cards.label: Rinse and hang
cards.text: A quick rinse after each shower and a hang to dry stops mildew starting. Choose it as the daily habit that makes the wash easier.

howToChoose.note: Skip the dryer, which can warp cups.

faq.q: Can I put a suction mat in the washing machine?
faq.a: Many are machine washable, as the listings say. Use a cold, gentle cycle, put the mat in a mesh bag and skip the dryer. Check the instructions for your mat. If the mat is large for your machine, a bathtub wash with warm soapy water and a soft brush is a good alternative, followed by a thorough rinse.

Heat can warp suction cups and soften the material, which weakens grip. Air dry the mat flat or hung. A towel under the mat helps it dry. A spare mat also gives you a clean one to put down when guests visit, which saves a last-minute scramble.

faq.q: How often should I wash a shower mat?
faq.a: A weekly rinse and a machine wash every two to four weeks suits most households. More often with heavy use or hard water. A mat that smells or feels slick is overdue. Put the mat in the machine with a couple of old towels, since they cushion it and balance the load.

faq.q: What if my mat has mildew stains?
faq.a: Wash it on cold and soak it briefly in a mild vinegar solution before rinsing. Dry it fully. If stains return quickly, replace the mat. Do not use bleach or fabric softener on a suction mat, because both can leave a film that weakens the cups.

Not if done gently. A clean mat grips better because the cups are free of film. Avoid harsh chemicals and heat. Check the cups after each wash by pressing the mat on a smooth surface, and retire it if they no longer hold.

faq.q: Should I keep a spare mat?
faq.a: It is a good idea, so that one can dry while the other is in use. A spare also avoids a day without a mat while one is in the wash. Hanging the mat over the shower rod or a towel bar lets air reach both sides and speeds drying.
